To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the force transmission efficiency can be improved by choosing the appropriate materials and by optimizing the design parameters of the Bowden cable.

i) the force transmission efficiency of the cable system can be improved by using smaller coefficient of friction materials, slower moving speed, smaller cable length, longer distance between the cable clamp and the cable end, and stiffer cable and sheath; and ii) the static friction ratio is a function of the coefficient of friction and the stiffness of cable and sheath.

a combination of 6×19 FEP coated stainless steel cable with double-sheath has the highest force efficiency, smaller coefficient of friction, smaller cable speed, longer cable length, longer clamping distance, and stiffer cable/sheaths all help to increase force efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the frictional properties of a Bowden cable.
the characterization of Bowden cables.
the experimental characterization of the Bowden cable friction, which is a fundamental problem in the field of cable actuated robots.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the force transmission efficiency is maximized when a small coefficient of friction material is chosen for the cable/sheath, the moving speed of the cable is small, the cable length is small, the clamp distance is large, the stiffness of the cable/sheath is large.

the Bowden cable friction is a complicated phenomenon and it is important for researchers to understand the underlying mechanisms of the friction in order to achieve high performance in their applications.

the friction of Bowden cable is a function of the coefficient of friction material between the cable and the sheath, the moving speed of the cable, the length of the cable, and the distance between two clamps, as well as the stiffness of the cable and the stiffness of the sheath.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Bowden cable friction is mainly determined by the coefficient of friction between cable and sheath.

the Bowden cable friction depends on the cable material, cable moving speed, cable length, cable/sheath stiffness, cable/sheath pretension, cable/sheath static friction, clamp distance, clamp stiffness and clamp friction.
the Bowden cable friction is a complex phenomenon that involves many variables and their interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the static friction pretensions of the cable/sheath pair should be as small as possible to increase the force transmissibility of the Bowden cables, and that the cable/sheath stiffness should be as large as possible.
the force transmission efficiency of Bowden cable is highly dependent on cable/sheath stiffness and the coefficient of friction.
Bowden cable friction can be reduced by increasing the cable/sheath stiffness, decreasing the cable moving speed, and increasing the cable pretension.
